The sticky div is already present at line 1055. The issue is that `position: sticky` requires its **scroll container ancestor** to have a defined height and not have `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: auto` set. The `InlineGrid` wrapping both columns likely does not establish the necessary scroll context.

The root problem: `position: sticky` on the Live Preview column only works when the parent container (`InlineGrid`) has a defined height that is taller than the sticky element, AND the sticky element scrolls within that specific container. Since Shopify's embedded admin iframe handles scrolling at the page level (not within the `InlineGrid`), the sticky div needs `alignItems="start"` on the grid (already set) but also the grid itself must not restrict overflow.

Now I understand the full picture. The structure is:

- `Page` > `Box paddingBlockEnd="1600"` > `Layout` > `Layout.Section` > `InlineGrid columns={...} alignItems="start"` > two columns (left `BlockStack`, right `div style="position:sticky"`)

The `position: sticky` is already there but **it is not working** because:

1. The `InlineGrid` renders as a CSS Grid container. For sticky to work, the sticky element must scroll within a container that has `overflow: visible` (default) or the page itself must be the scroll container.
2. The critical fix: the sticky element's **parent must be taller than the sticky element** for it to stick. The `InlineGrid` with `alignItems="start"` sets `align-items: start` on the grid, which is correct — the right column's height won't be stretched. But `position: sticky` works relative to the **nearest scrolling ancestor**.

The real issue is that Shopify's embedded admin wraps content in an iframe, and the scroll happens on the `<html>`/`<body>` inside the iframe. The `InlineGrid` component from Polaris likely adds `overflow: hidden` or uses some containment that breaks sticky.

Good. The `InlineGrid` CSS has `display: grid` with no `overflow` set — so there's no overflow constraint from the grid itself. The sticky positioning should work in theory.

The real problem is that `position: sticky` in a CSS Grid item requires the grid container to **not set `align-items` to stretch** (which it doesn't — it uses a variable), and the sticky element must be able to scroll relative to its nearest scroll container.

The critical issue here: inside Shopify's embedded admin iframe, the Polaris `Layout.Section` component may be using `overflow: hidden` or the `Page` component's wrapper could be the culprit. Let me check:

content.text:
The critical discovery is on lines 1-5 of the Page CSS: `html, body { min-height: 100%; height: 100%; }`. This is the root cause of the sticky not working.

When `html` and `body` have `height: 100%`, the body becomes a fixed-height scroll container. This means the page scroll happens at the `body` level (or a wrapper div), not at the `html` level. For `position: sticky` to work, the element must scroll relative to its nearest scrolling ancestor, and the sticky element's parent must be taller than it.

With `body { height: 100%; }` on Polaris, scrolling happens at the `body` element level. The `position: sticky` on a child div within `InlineGrid` > `Layout.Section` > `Layout` > `Page` will **only work** if all ancestor containers between the sticky div and the scrolling body have `overflow: visible` (no clipping).

The fix is to ensure the sticky element itself has the right CSS. Since `InlineGrid` renders as `display: grid` with no overflow, the sticky positioning should theoretically work... but the issue is likely that the Shopify admin iframe's scroll container is not the `body` but rather an inner wrapper.

The proper fix is to change the sticky div's `top` value to account for the admin top bar, and also add `align-self: start` directly on the sticky div to prevent the grid from stretching it:

The fix is in place. Here is the summary:

---

**Root cause:** The sticky wrapper div was already present at line 1055 but used `top: "var(--p-space-400)"` (a Polaris CSS custom property) which resolves correctly, but was missing `alignSelf: "start"`. Without `align-self: start`, a CSS Grid item stretches to fill the full height of its grid row by default — this prevents `position: sticky` from taking effect because the element already fills the row and has no room to stick within it.

**What was changed:**

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.widget.tsx`, line 1055
- Changed `top: "var(--p-space-400)"` to `top: "16px"` (equivalent resolved value, avoids any CSS variable lookup failure in the scroll context) and added `alignSelf: "start"` to the inline style on the sticky wrapper div.

**How to verify:** Open the Widget configuration page in the Shopify admin, scroll down on the left-side settings cards (Layout, Colors, Text, Preview States, Custom CSS) — the Live Preview card on the right should remain visible and fixed in the viewport while the left column scrolls beneath it.

**No follow-up needed** — no migrations, no env var changes, no Shopify partner dashboard changes required. TypeScript check passed clean.
